source: Yang et al. (2024) SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
finding: A custom agent-computer interface (ACI) made the same LM much better than a plain Linux shell. The ACI is a cognitive artifact built for the model.
numbers: GPT-4 Turbo: 12.47% (286/2294) on full SWE-bench; 18.00% (54/300) on Lite. Shell-only agent on Lite 10.7 points lower. Claude 3 Opus 10.46%. Prior non-interactive best 3.8%.
limits: Single benchmark; ACI tuned on GPT-4 Turbo; ablations on 300 Lite items with wide +/- margins.
agent_relevance: Interface design between code and model is worth more than prompt tweaks. Our code layer is the ACI.

source: Yang et al. (2024) SWE-agent ablation: editor with linting guardrail
finding: Blocking an edit that has a syntax error, and showing the error, raised success. No edit tool at all was worst.
numbers: Lite: edit with linting 18.0%; edit without linting 15.0 (-3.0); no edit tool 10.3 (-7.7). 51.7% of GPT-4 runs had 1+ failed edit. Any edit succeeds 90.5% of the time at first; odds fall as failed edits pile up.
quote: Linting is beneficial for stymieing cascading errors
limits: Differences of 3 points are near the noise of 300 items.
agent_relevance: Supports G2/G3: code checks the output and shows the real failure. Cheap code-side guardrails beat model self-checks.

source: Yang et al. (2024) SWE-agent ablation: viewer window, search, context
finding: Models are sensitive to how much the viewer shows. Too little or too much hurts. Summarised search beat iterative search.
numbers: Window 100 lines 18.0%; 30 lines 14.3 (-3.7); full file 12.7 (-5.3). Summarized search 18.0 vs iterative 12.0 (-6.0) vs no search 15.7. Last-5 observations 18.0 vs full history 15.0.
limits: Single model, single benchmark.
agent_relevance: Display size is a tunable artifact property. Show a bounded, summarised view, not raw dumps.

source: Yang et al. (2024) SWE-agent: edit failure and recovery behaviour
finding: Agents recover from failed edits more often than not, but each extra failure lowers the odds. 93.0% of resolved instances were submitted before the cost limit.
numbers: 1,185 of 2,294 trajectories (51.7%) had at least one failed edit.
limits: Trajectory statistics, not causal.
agent_relevance: Cap retries; after repeated failure change state, not just retry.

source: Yao et al. (2023) ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
finding: Letting the model interleave thoughts with tool actions beat acting alone and, on some tasks, chain of thought.
numbers: ALFWorld best ReAct 71% vs Act 45% vs BUTLER 37%; worst ReAct trial 48%. Relative gain over Act 33-90%, mean 62%. WebShop +10 absolute over prior best. Fever: ReAct 60.9 vs CoT 56.3; HotpotQA ReAct 27.4 vs CoT 29.4 (CoT better).
limits: Few-shot, PaLM-540B; ReAct lost on HotpotQA to CoT; search errors cause failures.
agent_relevance: Tool plus reasoning trace is the basic scaffold. The mixed result shows the tool is not always a gain.

source: Schick et al. (2023) Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
finding: A 6.7B GPT-J finetuned on self-labelled API calls (calculator, search, calendar, QA, translation) did much better zero-shot than same-size baselines and caught up with larger models on some tasks.
numbers: Base GPT-J 6.7B; tools: calculator, Wikipedia search, QA system, machine translation, calendar. Exact per-task scores not recorded.
limits: Cannot chain tools or use them interactively (own limitations section); table numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: Tools cover model weak spots (arithmetic, fresh facts). Use code for counting.

source: Gao et al. (2023) PAL: Program-aided Language Models
finding: The model writes the reasoning as Python and an interpreter runs it. This beat chain of thought, most when numbers were large.
numbers: GSM8K PAL (Codex) 72.0%, about 15 points over PaLM-540B CoT top-1; on GSM-HARD (big numbers) PAL beats CoT by about 40 absolute. SVAMP 79.4 vs 74.8.
limits: Depends on correct program; arithmetic word problems.
agent_relevance: The interpreter is an external calculating artifact; the model keeps the meaning, code does the work. Matches our program-decides rule.

source: Nye et al. (2021) Show Your Work: Scratchpads for Intermediate Computation
finding: Writing intermediate steps to a scratchpad (an external workspace) lifted multi-step computation a lot, even few-shot.
numbers: Polynomial evaluation: few-shot direct 8.8% vs scratchpad 20.1%; fine-tuned 31.8% vs 50.7%. Program execution: few-shot 11% vs 26.5%; fine-tuned 20% vs 41.5%.
limits: Small models, synthetic tasks; a scratchpad condition was slightly modified.
agent_relevance: The scratchpad is the written-notes artifact of Norman and Hutchins. Our states should keep explicit intermediate records.

source: Hsieh et al. (2023) Tool Documentation Enables Zero-Shot Tool-Usage with LLMs
finding: Good documentation of a tool did more than demonstrations. With docs, performance stays flat as demos are removed; without docs it falls.
numbers: Six tasks. LLM-Cloud command line (F1, 50 examples): zero-shot davinci-002 0.02, gpt-3.5-turbo 0.13; best few-shot 0.05 and 0.19; with documentation 0.37 and 0.45. ScienceQA docs-only beat docs plus 10-shot.
limits: Docs length limited by context; older models.
agent_relevance: The tool description is part of the artifact. Write the operator contract clearly instead of piling examples.

source: Patil et al. (2023) Gorilla: LLM Connected with Massive APIs
finding: A model tuned for API calls with retrieval of API docs hallucinated fewer wrong calls. A poor retriever hurt a lot.
numbers: Fine-tuned zero-shot 20.43% better than GPT-4, 10.75% better than ChatGPT on APIBench. Bad retriever (BM25, GPT-Index) lowered accuracy 21.50% (Torch Hub) and 47.57% (HuggingFace) at test time.
limits: Fine-tuned model; API names from three hubs.
agent_relevance: Bad retrieved context is worse than none. Artifact quality gates the gain.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Executable Code Actions Elicit Better LLM Agents (CodeAct)
finding: Code as the action format beat JSON or text actions on tool tasks, and tracebacks came for free as feedback.
numbers: Up to 20% absolute higher success than JSON/text across 17 LLMs on API-Bank and a new benchmark; up to 30% fewer actions. M3ToolEval gpt-4-0613 success 74.4% on first column of table.
limits: LLaMA-2 backbone tuning failed to help in one case; weaker models gain less.
agent_relevance: Code is a good interface language for a model; the interpreter gives real error output (G2).

source: Jimenez et al. (2024) SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
finding: Before better interfaces, the best model solved almost no real issues.
numbers: Best model Claude 2 solved 1.96% of issues in the non-interactive retrieval setup.
limits: Baseline setting; later agents with interfaces climbed far higher.
agent_relevance: Gives the before-interface baseline for the ACI effect.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
finding: A paged memory artifact (main context plus external store the model queries) lifted recall of old conversation.
numbers: Deep memory retrieval accuracy: GPT-4 32.1% to 92.5%; GPT-4 Turbo 35.3% to 93.4%; GPT-3.5 38.7% to 66.9%.
limits: Benchmark built by the authors; conversational recall only.
agent_relevance: External memory managed by code, queried when needed; analogue of ship navigation logs.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Storing a written reflection on a failed trial in an episodic buffer helped the next trial.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 91% vs GPT-4 baseline 80%.
limits: Relies on a real test signal.
agent_relevance: Written memory of real failure output only. Fits G2.

source: Ebouky et al. (2025) Eliciting Reasoning in Language Models with Cognitive Tools
finding: Giving the model cognitive operations as callable tools (understand question, recall related, examine answer, backtrack), each run by the same LLM, raised math scores.
numbers: GPT-4.1 AIME2024 pass@1 32.0 to 53.0 with tools; 42.0 with cognitive prompting. Gains from +4.2 (Qwen2.5-7B) to +27.2 (Llama3.3-70B). Understand-question tool called 80% of samples on AIME vs 14% on easier set.
limits: Maths only; GPT-4.1 as judge; limited prompt variants.
agent_relevance: Close to our operators O1-O8 as tool calls. Ours are code-sequenced; here the model chooses when.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
finding: Models use information best at the start or end of the context. Placement in the artifact matters.
numbers: U-shaped curve. GPT-3.5-Turbo closed-book 56.1%; oracle 88.3%. Accuracy lowest when the answer is in the middle of 20 documents.
limits: Retrieval QA and key-value tasks; older models.
agent_relevance: Put key state at the edges of the prompt; do not dump long history.

source: Tam et al. (2024) Let Me Speak Freely? Format Restrictions and LLM Performance
finding: Forcing JSON/XML output formats lowered reasoning accuracy; stricter formats hurt more.
numbers: Significant decline in reasoning tasks under format restriction; exact table numbers not recorded.
limits: Mixed across models and tasks; some classification tasks gain.
agent_relevance: The interface format has a cost. Let the model reason in free text, then parse into slots with code.

source: Sclar et al. (2024) Quantifying LMs' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design
finding: Meaning-preserving formatting changes change accuracy a lot.
numbers: Up to 76 accuracy points for LLaMA-2-13B between equivalent formats; persists with larger models, more shots and instruction tuning; weak correlation of best format between models.
limits: Mostly open models, few-shot.
agent_relevance: Format is an uncontrolled variable. Test any scaffold under several formats.

source: Kosmyna et al. (2025) Your Brain on ChatGPT: Cognitive Debt
finding: Essay writers with an LLM showed weaker EEG connectivity, lower ownership and weaker recall than search or no tool.
numbers: 54 participants, 18 per group (LLM, search, brain-only), 3 sessions; 18 did session 4.
limits: Small N, preprint, essay task only.
agent_relevance: Human side of the artifact. Not about agent quality; low weight.

source: Hesselmann & Gollo (2020) No conclusive evidence for a Google Stroop effect (replication)
finding: The 2011 Science 'Google Stroop' offloading result did not replicate.
numbers: Two replication attempts in a large project failed before this study; this one also found no conclusive evidence.
limits: Concerns one priming effect, not all offloading effects.
agent_relevance: Human offloading claims are weaker than popular accounts. Be careful borrowing them.

source: Kirsh & Maglio (1994) On Distinguishing Epistemic from Pragmatic Action
finding: Tetris players rotate and move pieces to learn what fits, not only to reach the goal. Acting in the world makes thinking cheaper.
numbers: Standard model compared to player data; exact timing ratios not recorded here.
limits: Single game task.
agent_relevance: Agent analogue: run code to find out instead of predicting. Epistemic actions are running tests or printing values.

source: Hutchins (1995) Cognition in the Wild
finding: Ship navigation is done by a system of people and tools, not one head. The tools hold computations.
numbers: Qualitative field study of a US Navy ship; no effect sizes.
limits: One setting, ethnography.
agent_relevance: Base theory: put memory and computation in artifacts that code controls.

source: Norman (1991) Cognitive artifacts
finding: An artifact changes the task the person faces (system view) versus what the person does (personal view).
numbers: Conceptual; no numbers.
limits: Theory chapter.
agent_relevance: The scaffold changes the model's task. Design for the task the model actually sees.

source: Qin et al. (2023) ToolLLM
finding: A large real-API corpus with a tool retriever and depth-first tool search gave a tuned LLaMA near ChatGPT on unseen tools.
numbers: 16,000+ real APIs; evaluated by pass rate and win rate (ToolEval). Exact numbers not recorded.
limits: Only abstract and figure caption seen; automatic judge.
agent_relevance: Tool retrieval is itself an artifact design choice.
